performance_protocol.purpose: Measure the checked-shift native packing fix on nonduplicate ROLLUP; keep the accepted public-ID planner and identical output values.
performance_protocol.inference: Use process medians, paired quartet log ratios and fixed seed 172 / 10000 bootstrap resamples. Retain all controls and observations.
performance_protocol.runtime: b0c39b8 optional runtime plus one native checked-shift fix
performance_protocol.input_limit: 512 integer keys and a nonduplicate grand total produce 513 sorted IDs. Duplicate and full-width correctness is covered separately in the SQL corpus.

performance_findings: All 160 processes retained, full counter coverage and zero migrations. Measurements use the ordinary release binaries; the separate checked integration build is not benchmarked.

ROLLUP execution instructions are unchanged to three decimal places in percent. Paired latency changes by -0.027 percent, interval [-0.058,-0.004], while same-binary execution controls move by +0.093 and +0.116 percent. No general speedup claim.

ROLLUP planning changes by -0.238 percent, interval [-0.563,0.087], with unchanged instruction work. Ordinary grouping planning changes by +0.987 percent while its same-parent-binary control moves +0.831 percent; instruction change is only +0.003 percent.
The checked shift has no measured material instruction increase on this input. Small timing shifts and all controls remain recorded; this is not proof of zero overhead on every grouping shape.
The preceding public GROUPING_ID planning cost of about 9 percent and earlier floating normalization/widening costs are outside this native-only comparison and remain open.
limitations: The native unit test body is compiled in a focused harness with the exact function body. The checked integration test uses the actual native crate through Sail; this is not a full native-crate unit suite.
The 64-bit capacity for semantic bits plus duplicate ordinals is unchanged. Existing capacity errors and duplicate rows are preserved.
This fix does not remove the preceding public GROUPING_ID planning cost or earlier floating normalization/widening costs.
Default vendored sources and the deferred type-inference shortcut remain unchanged.
